PHW style for gt tables

Source: R/gt.R
phw_gt_theme.Rd

phw_gt_theme() restyles an existing gt::gt() table: PHW font, navy title and column labels with a navy rule, light row lines and a bold source note. phw_gt() builds the table from a data frame (or a phw_summary_table() and friends) and adds the title, number formats and source line in one call.

Usage

phw_gt_theme(
  x,
  font_size = 14,
  accent = phw_colours[["navy"]],
  stripe = FALSE,
  ...
)

phw_gt(
  data,
  caption = NULL,
  subtitle = NULL,
  number = NULL,
  source = NULL,
  date = NULL,
  digits = 1,
  number_prefix = "Table",
  caption_args = list(),
  gt_args = list(),
  theme_args = list()
)

Arguments

x

A gt table.

font_size

Body font size in pixels.

accent

Colour of the title, column labels and rules.

stripe

Shade alternate rows?

...

Passed to gt::tab_options(), to change any other setting.

data

A data frame, or a summary table from phw_summary_table(), phw_crosstab(), phw_rate_table(), phw_risk_table() or phw_group_table(). Summary tables get bold group rows, indented levels and header spanners, as in phw_flextable().

caption

Table title.

subtitle

Optional subtitle.

number

Optional table number, giving "Table 1 ...".

source, date

Passed to phw_caption() and shown under the table.

digits

Decimal places for non-integer numbers.

number_prefix

Word before the number.

caption_args

List of other phw_caption() arguments.

gt_args

List of arguments for gt::gt(), e.g. list(groupname_col = "region").

theme_args

List of arguments for phw_gt_theme().

Value

A gt table.

Examples

if (requireNamespace("gt", quietly = TRUE)) {
  phw_gt(head(mtcars[, 1:4]), caption = "Example table", source = "mtcars")
  phw_gt_theme(gt::gt(head(iris)))
}
